subject: Tenant key retention notice and subprocessor scope clarification
messages:
From: Angela Park <angela.park@medicorps.com>

Cc: legal@medicorps.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant keys – retention window & subprocessor notification (Medicorps)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — Medicorps is interested in a Private (VPC) deployment with customer-held keys. Two quick compliance questions we need answered before our InfoSec team signs off: 

1) Retention/backup: if we provide a CMK (customer-managed key), what is Redwood's backup/retention policy for meta-data and telemetry associated with that tenant? We want assurance you do not keep long-lived copies of anything encrypted under our CMK beyond what is operationally necessary.

2) Subprocessor notification: if Redwood engages subprocessors for on-prem support or managed services (e.g., remote diagnostics, replacement hardware), will Medicorps be notified in advance and given an opportunity to approve (or require onshore-only)? What is the current list and the escalation process?

If you can provide a short runbook or a one-pager we can attach to the DPA, that would speed review.

Appreciate it —
Angela Park
Head of IT & Cloud Security
Medicorps Health

(attachment: summary_of_cloud_controls.pdf)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Angela Park <angela.park@medicorps.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant keys – retention window & subprocessor notification (Medicorps)

Hi Angela — great questions. Short answers up front, details below and I'm attaching the subprocessor matrix and a simplified data-flow slice.

1) Retention/backup: Redwood does not retain customer plaintext or key material for BYOK/private deployments. We retain limited telemetry (operation timestamps, anonymized request metrics) for 30 days by default for SRE/debugging and cost analysis; longer retention can be configured or disabled per contract. Any metadata stored is encrypted at rest and tied to your tenant identifier; we can include a retention clause in the DPA that sets the maximum telemetry retention to 0/30/90 days per Medicorps preference.

2) Subprocessors: For Private deployments we maintain a restricted subprocessor list. Operational subprocessors (hardware vendors, OEM support) are only engaged on an as-needed basis. Our standard process is: 10-day advance notice for any new subprocessor, with an option to require onshore-only providers for regulated workloads. We can add a contract clause to require notice + review period and to restrict certain categories (e.g., offshore remote support).

I'll loop in legal and product with the sample language we typically propose.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment stubs: redwood_subproc_matrix_v2.csv, data_flow_slice.png)

Subject: Fwd: Tenant keys – retention window & subprocessor notification (for DPA language)

Folks — forwarding Medicorps request. Points I think we should commit to in redline: 

- BYOK custody: confirm Redwood never escrows customer CMKs unless a separate escrow agreement is executed.
- Telemetry retention: offer two tiers in the DPA (default 30d, optional 0d for active compliance customers) and state data is encrypted with tenant-scoped keys.
- Subprocessor notifications: commit to 10-business-day notice + right to restrict/approve subprocessors that will have remote access to customer environments.
- Geo-restriction: where onshore-only is requested, provide list of allowable subprocessors (we may need to offer a premium contract amendment for guaranteed onshore support).

Soojin — product question: operationally, if a customer requires 0-day telemetry retention and onshore-only subproc, can we still offer remote diagnostics (we'd need to ship a hardware technician) or will we require on-prem engineer engagement?

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Tenant keys – retention window & subprocessor notification (Medicorps)

Hi Angela — thanks for the patience while we clarified internally. Summary of commitments we can include in the DPA appendix and next steps: 

1) BYOK custody: Redwood will not escrow or hold customer CMKs. Any requests for escrow will be handled via a separate signed escrow addendum.

2) Telemetry & retention: default telemetry retention = 30 days. Medicorps may elect a 0-day retention setting (no operational telemetry retained beyond ephemeral logs) at contract signature. We will also allow a temporary debugging retention (24–72 hours) if Medicorps explicitly authorizes it for a troubleshooting window—this will be logged and requires a named approver from Medicorps.

3) Subprocessor notification & approval: Redwood commits to a 10-business-day advance notice for any new subprocessor that could have remote access to the private deployment. Medicorps will have the right to require onshore-only subprocessors for categories that involve remote access; if Medicorps selects this option, Redwood will provide a cost estimate for the onshore support add-on.

4) Escalation & evidence: Redwood will provide an evidence bundle (audit logs, subproc attestations) via a secure Drive link within 5 business days of a verified request under the DPA; for urgent compliance reviews we can accelerate to 48 hours subject to a reasonable scope.

Next steps: 
- I will prepare a one-page DPA appendix (redlineable) with the language above and the metadata options (30d/0d retention, onshore add-on).
- Please confirm which telemetry retention option Medicorps prefers and whether you want onshore-only subprocessors as part of the baseline scope.

If that works I can route the appendix to DocuSign and include the subprocessor CSV we attached earlier for your legal team's review.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
